correctness.rationale: Leaf-permutation averaging preserves feasible convex sets and objective. A two-parameter Gram matrix has Schur complement eigenvalues 1-b and 1+(n-1)b-na^2; its maximum q is 2n*p(1-p)/(n-1), attained by a regular-simplex leaf residue, yielding R0. All metric triangles reduce to q<=2p and, when n>=3, q<=2/3, giving the exact transition at p=1/n and n=3 cap. A cut mixture is a random flipped-leaf subset with mean size <=n*epsilon and clique weight K(n-K); concave piecewise-linear interpolation and a uniform-size mixture give C sharply. The interpolation defect is alpha(1-alpha). Independently checked 198 rational (n,epsilon) pairs for n=2..12 with PSD Schur complement, triangles, cut chord and gap, including endpoints.
residual_risks: Comparator is a convex cut-polytope slice under individual expected hub-edge marginals, not the hull of individually constrained cuts.

value.rationale: An exact full-parameter gap between elliptope, metric triangle strengthening, and cut-polytope feasible moments on a natural rooted star plus clique is a useful structural benchmark. It identifies the first positive-gap graph size (five vertices) and a sharp universal 1/4 additive defect within this family; neither correctness nor reproducibility alone is used as the value argument.
residual_risks: Not a worst-case weighted MaxCut integrality-ratio or algorithmic speedup theorem; deterministic-margin interpretation is explicitly excluded.

final_claim: For n>=2 leaves, epsilon in [0,1/2], maximize the unit leaf-clique cut objective over a star-conditioned correlation elliptope, over its intersection with all metric triangles, and over the cut polytope with matching marginal hub constraints. The exact three support optima are R0=n^2*eps*(1-eps), the stated piecewise Rtriangle, and C=linear interpolation of k(n-k) at n*eps; Rtriangle-C is 0 for n<=3 or eps<=1/n and otherwise frac(n*eps)*(1-frac(n*eps)), attaining 1/4.
